translations.text: In the first year of the reign of Cyrus king of Persia, when the word of the Lord spoken through Jeremiah was fulfilled, the Lord stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia. He issued a proclamation throughout his kingdom and also put it in writing, saying:
“This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The Lord, the Lord of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and he has directed me to build him a house in Jerusalem in Judah.
Whoever is among all the peoples, may the Lord be with him, so that he may go up to Jerusalem in Judah and build the house of the Lord, the God of Israel. He is the Lord who is in Jerusalem.

And all who remain in any of the districts where he himself deported them are to be helped by the people of that region with gold, silver, goods, and livestock, as well as whatever they willingly give for the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.”

Then the heads of the ancestral families of Judah and Benjamin, the priests, the Levites, and all those in whose hearts God had placed the desire to go up and build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem arose.
Everyone around them helped them with articles of gold and silver, livestock, and other things they contributed willingly.
King Cyrus also brought out the articles belonging to the house of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem and brought into the house of his god.
Cyrus king of Persia brought them out through Mithredath son of Gazabar, who recorded them and handed them over to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.
These were their numbers: thirty gold basins, one thousand silver basins, and twenty-nine bowls.
There were thirty gold cups, four hundred and ten silver cups, and one thousand other articles.
All the gold and silver articles numbered five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brought all these up with those who came up from captivity [?] from Babylon to Jerusalem.

These are the people of the province who went up to Jerusalem and returned from the place where they had been taken captive and exiled, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported to Babylon, and who returned to Jerusalem.

And the people of Judah entered their cities, those who had come out with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah. This was the number of the people of Israel:
The descendants of Parosh: 2,172.
The descendants of Shephatiah: three hundred and seventy-two.
The descendants of Arah: seven hundred and seventy-five.
And the descendants of Pahath-moab, those descended from Jeshua and Joab: 2,812.
The descendants of Elam: one thousand two hundred and fifty-four.
The descendants of Zattu: nine hundred and forty-five.
The descendants of Zaccai: seven hundred and sixty.
The descendants of Bani: six hundred and forty-two.
The descendants of Bebai: six hundred and twenty-two.
The descendants of Azgad: one thousand two hundred and twenty-two.
The descendants of Adonikam: six hundred and sixty-six.
The descendants of Bigvai: two thousand and fifty-six.
The descendants of Adin: four hundred and fifty-four.
The descendants of Ater, of Hezekiah: ninety-eight.
The descendants of Bezai: three hundred and twenty-three.
The descendants of Jorah: 112.
The descendants of Hashum: 223.
The descendants of Gibbar: 95.
The people of Bethlehem: 123.
The people of Netophah: 56.
The people of Anathoth: 128.
The descendants of Azmaveth: 42.
The people of Kiriath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth: 743.
And the people of Ramah and Geba: 621.
And the people of Michmash: 122.
The people of Bethel and Ai: 223.
And the people of Nebo: 52.
The descendants of Magbish: 156.
The descendants of Erim: 1,254.
The descendants of Elam: 320.
And the descendants of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, and the descendants of Hadid and Ono: 725.
The people of Jericho: 345.
The descendants of Senaah: 3,630.
And the priests: the descendants of Jedaiah, who were from the house of Jeshua: 973.
And the descendants of Immer: 1,052.
The descendants of Pashhur: 1,247.
And the descendants of Harim: 1,017.
And the Levites: the descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel, from the descendants of Hodaviah: 74.
And the singers: the descendants of Asaph: 128.

And the descendants of the gatekeepers—the descendants of Shallum, the descendants of Ater, the descendants of Talmon, the descendants of Akkub, the descendants of Hatita, and the descendants of Shobai—139 in all.
The temple servants: the descendants of Ziha, the descendants of Hasupha, and the descendants of Tabbaoth.
The descendants of Kades, the descendants of Siaha, the descendants of Padon.
The descendants of Lebanah, the descendants of Hagabah, the descendants of Akkub.
The descendants of Hagab, the descendants of Shalmai, the descendants of Hanan.
The descendants of Giddel, the descendants of Gahar, the descendants of Reaiah.
The descendants of Rezin, the descendants of Nekoda, the descendants of Gazzam.
The descendants of Uzza, the descendants of Paseah, the descendants of Besai.
The descendants of Asnah, the descendants of Meunim, the descendants of Nephusim.
The descendants of Bakbuk, the descendants of Hakupha, and the descendants of Harhur.
The descendants of Bazluth, the descendants of Mehida, the descendants of Harsha.
The descendants of Barkos, the descendants of Sisera, the descendants of Temah.
The descendants of Neziah, the descendants of Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon’s servants: the descendants of Sotai, the descendants of Hassophereth, the descendants of Peruda.
The descendants of Jaalah, the descendants of Darkon, the descendants of Giddel.
The descendants of Shephatiah, the descendants of Hattil, the descendants of Pochereth, the descendants of Hazzebaim, the descendants of Ami.
All the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon’s servants numbered 392.
These were the ones who came up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer, but could not identify their ancestral families and their lineage to establish whether they were Israelites.
The descendants of Delaiah, the descendants of Tobiah, and the descendants of Nekoda numbered 652.

And from the priestly families: the descendants of Habaiah, the descendants of Hakkoz, and the descendants of Barzillai, who married a woman from among the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite and was called by their name.
They sought to have them registered among those enrolled by genealogy, but they did not find them, and they removed them from their priesthood.
And the governor [?] that they were not to eat any of the most holy things until a high priest was appointed who wears the Urim and arranges them for the perfect ones.
Their entire assembly numbered 42,360, apart from their male and female servants.
These servants numbered 7,336.
There were also 200 male and female singers.
Their horses numbered 736, and their mules numbered 245.
Their camels numbered 435, and their donkeys numbered 6,720.
Some of the heads of their ancestral families, when they reached the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, made voluntary offerings for the house of the Lord, for the work they would do on it.
According to their ability, they brought into the treasury for the expenses of the work 61,000 minas of refined gold, 5,000 minas of silver, and 100 priestly garments.
The priests, the Levites, the people, the singers, the gatekeepers, and the temple servants settled in their respective towns, and Israel settled in their towns.
When the seventh month arrived, Israel was living in their cities. Then the people gathered together in Jerusalem as one person.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his brothers, arose and built the altar of the God of Israel, to offer sacrifices on it as written in the Law of Moses, the man of God.

They built the altar according to its prescribed arrangement, because fear of the peoples of the land had come upon them. They offered sacrifices on it to the Lord, both in the morning and in the evening.

They celebrated the Feast of Booths as it was written, and offered the sacrifices in the number prescribed for each day, according to the regulations for the people, at their appointed times, day by day.
After this came the regular sacrifices, those at each new moon and at all the Lord’s holy festivals, and those of everyone who voluntarily made a vow to the Lord.
From the beginning of the seventh month they began bringing sacrifices to the Lord, but the foundation of the Lord’s house had not yet been laid.

They gave gold to the carpenters and stonecutters, and food, drink, and oil to the people of Tyre and Sidon, so that they would bring them cedar timber from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa and return from there, under the command that Cyrus king of Persia had given them.

In the second year after they reached Jerusalem, at the house of the Lord, in the second month, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Jeshua son of Jozadak, the rest of their brothers—the priests and Levites—and everyone who had come to Jerusalem from captivity began the work. They appointed the Levites twenty years old and older to oversee the work on the Lord’s house.

Jeshua and his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, and the sons of Judah took their places over those working on the Lord’s house, along with the sons of Henadad, their sons, and their brothers, the Levites.

They laid the foundation to build the house of the Lord. The priests stood in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites, the descendants of Asaph, praised the Lord with cymbals as they laid the foundation of the house of the Lord, according to the instruction of David, king of Israel.

They responded with praise and thanksgiving to the Lord, saying, “For he is good, and his mercy toward Israel lasts forever.” All the people cried out loudly and praised the Lord as the foundation of the Lord’s house was laid.

Many of the priests, Levites, representatives of their ancestral families, and elders who knew the former house wept loudly when they laid its foundation and saw this house with their own eyes. And many shouted with cries of celebration as they spoke.
No one among the people could distinguish the sound of joyful shouting from the cries of their weeping, because the people shouted so loudly that it could be heard far away.
The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the descendants of the exiles were building a house for the Lord, the God of Israel.

They went to Zerubbabel and the leaders of their ancestral families and said to them, “Let us also build with you, because we seek your God as you do. We too have obeyed him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Persia, who brought us here.”

Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of the leaders of Israel’s ancestral families said to them, “It is not for you and us to build the house of our God together. We ourselves will build it on our own for the Lord our God, as Cyrus king of Persia commanded us.”
The peoples of the land began to obstruct the people of Judah and frighten them out of building.
They hired people against them to make them abandon their plans throughout the days of Cyrus king of Persia, until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
During the reign of Ahasuerus, at the beginning of his reign, they wrote a letter against those living in Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of their servants wrote a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia. Its translation was in Aramaic.
Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter of accusation against Jerusalem and sent it to King Artaxerxes.

They said, “We speak as follows: Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of the servants of our lords—the Dinaites, Apharsathchites, Tarpelites, Apharsites, Archevites, Babylonians, Susanchites, Elamites, and Dehavites—
“and the rest of the peoples whom the great and honored Osnappar deported and settled in the towns of Samaria, and those beyond the River.”
The letter they wrote to King Artaxerxes said this: “We are your servants, the people beyond the River.

“Let their lord the king know that the Jews who came up from you to us have arrived in Jerusalem, the rebellious and wicked city, to rebuild it. They are restoring its walls and raising its foundations.

“Now let their lord the king know that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are erected, you will have no tribute, and they will make no payments to you, because it is rebellious against the kingdom.
“It is not right for us to watch them dishonor the king. For this reason we have sent word so that their lord the king may know.

“Search the books of the records of your ancestors, and you will find and learn that this city is rebellious and causes trouble for kings and provinces. Rebellion by servants has been within it since ancient times, from the beginning. For this reason this city was laid waste.”
The messenger whom you sent has reached me.
I ordered them to search in the book of [?], and we found that it is hostile and wrongs whoever enters it.
Mighty kings also reigned in Jerusalem and ruled the whole region beyond the River, and taxes and tribute were paid to them.
And now restrain those men so that they do not build that city. From now on, keep watch over them.
Take care not to neglect them in this matter, so that its destruction does not increase and they do not harm the kings.

When Artaxerxes’ messenger arrived, he read it before Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the servants of their masters who were with them. They hurried on horseback to Jerusalem and Judah and forced them to stop.
Then the construction of the house of the Lord in Jerusalem was stopped, and it remained suspended until the second year of the reign of Darius, king of Persia.
Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo the prophet prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem. They prophesied to them in the name of the God of Israel.
At that time Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God in Jerusalem. The prophets of Israel were with them, helping them.

Then, at that time, Tattenai, the governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and the servants of their masters came to them and said, “Who commanded you to build this house, and who gave you permission to do this?”
They asked them their names and said to them, “Who are you men who are building this city?”

For God had mercy on the captives of Judah and watched over them. They did not hinder them until a letter came back from Darius, nor did they trouble them. Then they sent a messenger about that matter.

They made their inquiry in the letter sent by Tattenai, the governor of the region beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and the servants of their masters, the Apharsachites beyond the River. They sent the letter to King Darius.
This is the message written in the letter: “Peace to King Darius.

“So that you may know everything, O king, their lord: we went to the land of Judah, to the house of the great God. We found them building with fine stone and with a foundation of remarkable [?], which they put in its place. The work is progressing quickly in their hands.
“We questioned their leaders and said to them, ‘Who commanded you to build, and who gave you permission to do this?’
We also asked them their names so that we could write to you, so that you might know the names of those men and of their leaders.

They gave us this answer, saying, “We are servants of the Lord, the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding this house, which was built long ago, many years before. A great king of Israel built it and erected it for them.
But when our ancestors provoked the God of heaven, he handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon. He demolished the house and deported the people to Babylon.
“In the first year of his reign, King Cyrus commanded that they build that house of God.

“Cyrus also took from his royal palace the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of that house in Jerusalem and placed in his royal palace. He gave them to Sheshbazzar, his treasurer and administrator.
“He said to him, ‘Take these vessels, go, and put them in the house in Jerusalem, in their place.’
“Then Sheshbazzar came, and he himself laid the foundation of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that time until now they have been building it, and it has not been completed.”

And now, if the king wishes, let a search be made in the treasury of the king of Babylon, so that you may know that King Cyrus ordered this house of the Lord in Jerusalem to be built. And, having considered it, lord king, send us what you wish.”
Then King Darius ordered them to open the books of their [?] in the treasury in Babylon.
In the city of Bari they found a scroll, and in it was written a memorandum saying:

“In the first year of his reign, King Cyrus issued a command concerning the temple of God in Jerusalem: the house was to be rebuilt, including the place of sacrifice where sacrifices are offered. He ordered its height to be sixty cubits and its width sixty cubits.
“They are to build it in courses, with three courses of stone and one course of timber. Their expenses are to be paid from the royal treasury.

“The gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took out of that house in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, are to be given back and placed in the temple in Jerusalem, in the place where they had been in the house of God.”
He commanded Tattenai and Shethar-bozenai, the governors of the region beyond the River, and the servants of their masters, the Apharsachites beyond the River, saying:
“Let the house of God be built. Let the leaders of Judah carry out the work on the house of God and build it on its site.

“I have commanded: take care not to do anything to the leaders of Judah or prevent them from building the house of God. Give these men their expenses from the royal treasury, out of the taxes of the region beyond the River, and do not trouble them.

“Take care and do not fail: give them young cattle, sheep, and goats for sacrifice to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil, in the amounts the priests in Jerusalem tell you. Give them these things whenever they ask you,
“so that they may present offerings and sacrifices to the God of heaven and pray for the life of the king and the lives of his children.”

I have also decreed that, for anyone who violates this command of mine, a timber shall be taken from his house, and he shall be hung on it and killed. I have decreed that his house shall likewise be treated in the same way.

May the God who has caused his name to dwell there overthrow all kings and nations who transgress this decree of mine and who raise their hands to alter and destroy the house of the Lord in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have commanded that they do this and carry it out diligently.
Then Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai, and the servants of their masters who were with them did as King Darius had instructed them, without delay.

The elders of the Jews and the Levites continued building while Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to them. They built and established it by the command of the God of Israel and by the command of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, king of Persia.
They finished that house on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of Darius's reign.
The people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the descendants of the exiles celebrated the dedication of the house of the Lord with joy.

For the dedication of the house of the Lord, they brought one hundred cattle, two hundred rams, four hundred young goats, and twelve male goats as a sin offering on behalf of all Israel, according to the number of the tribes of Israel.
They appointed the priests according to their prescribed duties and the Levites alongside their companions to serve the Lord in Jerusalem, as written in the book of Moses.
The descendants of the exiles celebrated the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.

The priests and the Levites purified themselves, and all of them were clean. They slaughtered the Passover sacrifice for all the descendants of the exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.
The Israelites who had returned from exile ate with joy, together with all who had joined them, leaving the uncleanness of the nations of the land to seek the Lord, the God of Israel.

They celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with joy, because the Lord had made them joyful and had turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, strengthening their hands for the work on the house of the God of Israel.
After these events, during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia, [?] Ezra, son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hacaliah.
The son of Shallum, the son of Zadok, the son of Ahitub.
Son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth.
Son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki.
Son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, the priest from among their ancestors.

He went up from Babylon to Jerusalem. Ezra was knowledgeable in the law of Moses, which the Lord, the God of Israel, had given. The king granted him everything he desired, because the hand of the Lord his God was with him.
Some of the people of Israel, and some of the priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants, went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of the reign of King Artaxerxes.
They arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king's reign.
In the first month they began their journey up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month they arrived in Jerusalem, because the gracious hand of the Lord his God was upon him.
For Ezra had set his heart on studying the law of the Torah, practicing it, and teaching Israel justice and judgment.
This is the decree in the letter that Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest, the scribe of the book of the commandments of the Lord's word and of his judgments, which he had given to Israel.
He said: I, Artaxerxes, king of kings, have sent this to Ezra, the scribe of the law of the Lord, the God of heaven.
I have issued a decree that all among the Israelites, the priests, and the Levites who wish to go to Jerusalem may go with you.
The king and his seven counselors gave orders and sent them to examine matters in Judah and Jerusalem according to the law of their God, which is in your hand.
The king and his counselors sent gold and silver for the house of the Lord, the God of Israel, who dwells in Jerusalem.
Also, all the other gold and silver found throughout the territory of Babylon, together with the offerings that the people and the priests brought for the house of the Lord in Jerusalem.
I have commanded all this in this letter, and also cattle, sheep, and lambs for the sacrifices and drink offerings to be made on the altar of the house of their God in Jerusalem.
With the gold and silver that remain, make your people rejoice, and do what pleases your God. Do this with what remains.
Bring the vessels that I have given for the service of the house of the Lord before the Lord in Jerusalem.
And whatever else you need for the house of the LORD, you shall provide from the treasury of my kingdom.
I, King Artaxerxes, command all the treasurers beyond the River: provide everything that Ezra, the priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven, asks of you.
Up to one hundred talents of silver, one hundred cors of wheat, one hundred measures of wine, one hundred measures of oil, and salt without limit.
Let everything be done according to the law of the God of heaven. Take care not to harm the house of the God of heaven, so that wrath does not come upon the king’s kingdom and upon his children.
And you also, priests and Levites, all of you, sing. As for the temple servants, the gatekeepers, and those who work in the house of the LORD, take no tribute and do not subject them to servitude.
And you, Ezra, according to the wisdom of God that is upon you, appoint scribes and [?] to judge all the people beyond the River and all those who know the law of God. Teach those who do not know it.
Anyone who does not obey the law of God and the law of the king shall be judged immediately, whether sentenced to death, confiscation of property, flogging, or forced labor.
Ezra said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of our fathers, who put it into the king’s heart to honor his house in Jerusalem.”

He extended his mercy to me before the king, his counselors, and all the king’s high officials. I took courage because the blessed hand of the LORD was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
These are the heads of their ancestral families who were listed to go up with me from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.
From the descendants of Phinehas, Gershom; from the descendants of Ithamar, Daniel; and from the descendants of David, Hattush.
From the descendants of Shecaniah, and from the descendants of Parosh: Zechariah, and with him one hundred fifty men who were registered.
From the descendants of Pahath-moab, Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and with him two hundred men.
From the descendants of Zattu: Shecaniah son of Azel, and with him three hundred men.
From the descendants of Adin: Ebed son of Jonathan, and with him fifty men.
From the descendants of Elam: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, and with him seventy men.
From the descendants of Shephatiah, Zebadiah son of Michael, and with him eighty men.
From the descendants of Joab: Obadiah son of Jehiel, and with him two hundred eighteen men.
From the descendants of Bani: Shelomith son of Josiphiah, and with him one hundred sixty men.
From the descendants of Bebai: Zechariah son of Bebai, and with him twenty-eight men.
From the descendants of Azgad: Johanan son of Hakkatan, and with him one hundred ten men.
From the descendants of Adonikam, the last ones, whose names were Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah, and with them sixty men.
From the descendants of Bigvai: Uthai and Zabbud, and with them seventy men.
I gathered them beside the river that flows toward Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I inspected the people and the priests, but we found no descendants of Levi there.
I sent for Eleazar son of Ariel, Shemaiah, Halonam, Jarib, Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam, who were leaders, and for Joiarib and Elnathan, who were men of understanding.

I took them to Iddo the chief and gave them gold. I put words in their mouths to speak to Iddo and his brothers, the temple servants in the place called Casiphia, so that they would bring us singers for the house of our God.
Because the good hand of our God was upon us, they brought us a wise man from the descendants of Mahli son of Levi, son of Israel, and Serkiah with his sons and brothers, eighteen in all.
Hashabiah and Jeshaiah, from the descendants of Merari, together with his brothers and sons, were twenty.
And from the temple servants whom David and their leaders had appointed to serve the Levites, there were two hundred twenty temple servants. I gathered each of them by name.
I proclaimed a fast for them beside the river Ahava, so that we might humble ourselves before our God and so that he might prepare our journey for us, our children, and all our possessions.

For I was ashamed to ask the king for troops and horses to save us from enemies along the way, because we had told the king, “The hand of our God brings good to all who seek him, but his power and wrath are against all who forsake him.”
We fasted and prayed to our God about this, and he heard us.
I set apart twelve of the leaders of the priests: Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and ten of their brothers with them.
I weighed out for them the gold, silver, and vessels for the house of our God that the king, his counselors, his officials, and all the Israelites who were there had previously sent.
I weighed them out into their hands and gave them six hundred and fifty talents of silver, one hundred talents of gold, and one hundred silver vessels.
And twenty gold bowls, these [?], nine thousand, and iron vessels, carved and fine, each plated with gold.
I said to them, “You are holy to the LORD, and these vessels are holy. The gold and silver are an offering to the LORD, the God of our fathers.”

Be watchful, then, and guard them until you weigh them out before their officials, the priests and Levites, and the heads of their ancestral families in Jerusalem, in the courtyard of the house of the Lord.
I weighed them out for them and gave the priests and Levites the silver shekels, the gold, the silver, and the articles, according to their number, to take to Jerusalem for the house of our God.

Then we departed from the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the waxing moon in the first month, to go to Jerusalem. The hand of our God was with us, and he saved us from the power of our enemies who fought against us along the way.
We reached Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.

On the fourth day we weighed all the gold, silver, and vessels in the house of our God and entrusted them to Meremoth son of Uriah the priest. With him was Eleazar son of Phinehas, and with them were Jozabad son of Joses and Noadiah son of Binnui, who were Levites.
We counted everything for them and weighed it, and that day we recorded its entire weight.

Those who had returned from the place where they had been taken captive, the descendants of the exiles, brought sacrifices to the Lord of Israel: twelve oxen for all Israel, ninety-six sheep, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve female goats as a sin offering. All their sacrifices were for the Lord.
I gave the king’s letter to the king’s administrators and to the officials beyond the River, and they honored the people and the house of the Lord.

After this was finished, the officials of the people came to me and said, “The people of Israel, the priests, and the Levites have not separated themselves from the peoples of the land and the uncleanness of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.”
He took a wife from among their daughters, and they married off their sons. The holy offspring mingled with the people of the land, and the officials were the first to join them in this sin.
When I heard this report, I tore my clothing and my cloak, mourned, and pulled out hair from my head and beard. Then I sat in grief and lowered my face.
All those who feared the Lord came to me, speaking to me the word of the God of Israel concerning this wrongdoing of the exiles. I sat in grief until the time of the evening sacrifice.
When the time of the evening sacrifice came, I rose in my distress, after tearing my clothes and my cloak. I knelt on my knees and raised my hands to the Lord my God.
I said, “Lord, I am ashamed to lift my face to you, because our sins are many and rise above the hair of our heads, and our wrongdoing has grown great and reached heaven.

From the days of our fathers until today we have been greatly guilty. Because of our sins, we, our kings, our priests, and our children were taken captive and fell into the hands of the kings of the nations. They killed us with their swords, took us captive, and plundered us, and we remain ashamed to this day.

And now we have had a little rest, when our God showed us mercy, preserved us, gave us life, and gave us strength in his holy house, so that our God might brighten our eyes and [?] us a little from our bondage.

For we are his servants. Our God has not abandoned us, but has given us favor before the kings of Persia, so that they might give us our sustenance, honor our holy house, rebuild the ruins of Zion, and give us strength in Judah and Jerusalem.
And now, Lord, what shall we say? While you give to them, they have disobeyed your commandment.

Which you gave through your servants the prophets, saying to them, ‘The land that you are entering to possess is unclean because of the foulness of the peoples of the land, and they have filled it with their uncleanness.

Now, do not give your daughters in marriage to their sons, and do not give their daughters in marriage to your sons. Do not hate them, and do not be friendly with them forever, so that you may be strong, eat the blessings of the land, and leave it as an inheritance to your children forever.’
All this has come upon us because of our evil deeds and the greatness of our sins. For you, our God, have [?] us from our sins, so that we might turn back and keep the remainder of your commandment.
For we have again transgressed your commandment and entered into marriage alliances with the nations. Do not be angry with us forever, leaving none of us who escapes.
Lord, God of Israel, you are righteous, you who have preserved us and saved us today, on this day. Here we are before you in sin, for no one can stand before you because of this.”

When Ezra finished his prayer and confession, weeping as he prayed before the house of the Lord, many men from Israel gathered around him. There was a great assembly, together with their wives and their young people, and the people wept bitterly.

Shecaniah son of Jehiel, one of the descendants of Elam, answered and said to Ezra, “We ourselves have sinned against our God by marrying foreign women from the land. Yet even now there is hope for Israel concerning this.

But let us make a covenant with our God, and [?] Israel now concerning this, so that they send away their wives together with the children they have borne them. Arise and rebuke them as you wish, according to the commandment of our God, and let them act according to our law.
Rise, for this matter is your responsibility, and we are with you. Be strong and act.”
Ezra rose and made the officials, the priests, the Levites, and all Israel swear to do as he had commanded them, and they swore.

Ezra rose from before the house of the Lord and went toward the chamber [?]. Johanan son of Eliashib went there with him. He ate no food and drank no water, because he was mourning over the sins and transgressions of the exiles.

He proclaimed to them, among the officials throughout Judah and Jerusalem, saying, “Anyone who does not arrive within three days, as the officials and leaders have commanded, shall have all his property destroyed, and they shall exclude him from the assembly of the exiles.”
All the men of Judah and Benjamin assembled in Jerusalem within those three days, in the ninth month, on the fifth day of the waning moon.
All the people sat in the open square of the house of the Lord, trembling because of this matter and because of the rainy season, for rain was falling.
Then Ezra the priest stood up and said to them, “You have sinned by marrying foreign women, and you have added sin to the sin of Israel.”
Now praise the Lord, the God of our fathers, and do what is good before him. Separate yourselves from the nations of the land and from the foreign women.
All the people answered and said, “This is a great task for us to carry out.”
“But the people are many, and it is the rainy season in the land. We cannot finish dealing with them now, for this is not the work of one day or two days, since we have sinned greatly in this matter.

Instead, let all the representatives of our people from all our towns who have married foreign women come, and let the elders of our towns and our judges assemble with them in their presence, so that the fierceness of our God’s anger, which has come upon us because of this matter, may turn away from us.”
But Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahzeiah son of Tikvah are with me in this matter, and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite help them.

The descendants of the exiles did so. Ezra the priest selected men who were heads of their ancestral families, according to their households, all designated by name. They sat down on the first day of the tenth month to investigate the matter.
He finished dealing with all the men who had married foreign women by the first day of the first month.
Among the descendants of the priests, these were found to have married foreign women: from the descendants of Joash son of Jozadak and his brothers, Maaseiah, Eleazar, Orem, and Gedaliah.
They gave their pledge to send away their wives and to bring rams because of their guilt and offer them as a sacrifice.
From the descendants of Immer: Hanani and Zebadiah.
From the descendants of Harim: Masahel, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.
From the descendants of Pashhur: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Shemeel, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.
From among the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, and Kolaiah—Koliath himself—and Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.
From among the singers: Eliashib. From among the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.
From Israel, from the descendants of Parosh: Ramiah, Izziah, Malchijah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.
From the descendants of Elam: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Elijah.
From the descendants of Zattu: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.
From the descendants of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.
From the descendants of Bani: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.
From the descendants of Pahath-moab: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.
From the descendants of Harim: Eliezer, Isshijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Simeon, Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.
From the descendants of Hashum: Mattaniah, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.
And from the descendants of Bani: Maadai, Amram, Uel, Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluh, Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Mattenai, and Jaasu.
The descendants of Bani and the descendants of Shimei: Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah, Malchinedabai, Shashai, and Seraiah.
And Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah, Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.
From the descendants of Nebo: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jabdu, Joel, and Benaiah.
All these had married foreign women, and some of these women had borne children to them.
